justification: Consignment FF-8003 corresponds to a single shipment, SH-4003 (Pune to Kolhapur, delivered once on 2026-07-06), yet it was billed in full on two separate Falcon invoices (07A and 07B), each at the same amount and each individually matching the contract-computed expected charge for that one shipment under §1's per-km, weight-banded base freight (plus applicable premiums/surcharges). The shipment record shows no second movement, no re-delivery, and no split shipment that would justify a second charge, and nothing in the evidence (no credit note, no correction reference under §8) explains a legitimate second occurrence. Since the contract's freight charge is for carriage actually rendered on a given consignment, and only one carriage occurred, the second billing of the same consignment has no contractual basis and represents a duplicate charge that should not be paid twice.

memo_narrative.what_happened: Consignment FF-8003, tied to a single shipment (SH-4003), appears as a full line item on two separate Falcon invoices (07A and 07B) at the same billed figure.
memo_narrative.why: Only one carriage movement occurred for this consignment per the shipment record, and nothing in the evidence (no credit note under §8, no re-delivery or split shipment) supports a second legitimate charge for the same freight under §1's base freight terms or the §5 accessorial whitelist.
memo_narrative.recommended_action: Contact Falcon to confirm this is a duplicate posting and request a credit note under §8 removing the second occurrence, retaining only one payable instance of FF-8003.
